applicable_when: The kernel is a convolution bias-add that performs a layout transpose: input is NHWC-like (stride order: N=290400, C=1, H=5280, W=96) while output is NCHW (stride order: N=290400, C=3025, H=55, W=1). The load index y0 + 96*x2 + 290400*y1 strides by 96 in the X (thread) dimension, so 128 threads in XBLOCK each access elements 96 apart — severely non-coalesced. The store x2 + 3025*y3 is contiguous in x2 and benefits from vectorization. L2 is at 96% utilization (the bottleneck), and 70.9% of scheduler cycles have no eligible warp due to L1TEX load stalls. Adding tl.max_contiguous/tl.multiple_of hints on the output pointer enables the compiler to emit 128-bit vectorized stores. Switching to @triton.autotune explores tile shapes that better hide load latency — in particular, larger YBLOCK (more channel parallelism, which IS contiguous in the input) and smaller XBLOCK can improve input coalescing since y0 (channel) is stride-1 in the input.
